Consider the triangle $△ABC$ shown above. The line segment $\overset{―}{AH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overset{―}{BC}.$ If $m∠ACB={125}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠HAC.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠ACB & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{125}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA & ={55}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $△AHC$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC & ={180}^{∘} \\ {55}^{∘}+m∠HAC+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC+{145}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC & ={35}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
